summary: Both findings closed with honest tests: drain discard releases presence and handoff still transmits once; inbound observe errors now fail closed and silent.
notes: RE-ADJUDICATION after both fix_tasks were applied. contract-check re-run on the amended 02-contract.yaml: ok=true, violations=[]; not_checked: forbid.behaviors (manually reviewed). Totals 1674/1900; salida.go 69/110 (cap amended 20->110 by the orchestrator, PAT-022), traduccion.go 169/200, shared test glob 973/1100, 14/14 files. Verify harness re-ran green: 7/7 RC=0, 5 stability reps, go test -race clean.

FINDING 1 (drain-time leak) CLOSED. salida.go gains a ControlDeCortacircuitos field plus a nil-legal ConCortacircuitos chaining setter (deliberately not a constructor-signature change, so the forbidden outbox test files did not need migration) and a drain-time SalidaPermitida recheck in intentarUno, placed after the baja recheck and before verificarDisciplina. Tripped rows are hard-deleted with ContadorDescartadasPorCortacircuitos + EventoSalidaDescartadaPorCortacircuitos + liberarPresencia. Read errors DEFER the row rather than discard it (ContadorAplazadasPorErrorCortacircuitos + log), which is fail-closed and non-destructive, and does not burn a retry since it returns before registrarFallo; unbounded deferral is bounded by the existing TTL.

FINDING 1 verified against the three questions asked. (a) Presence release on every exit: liberarPresencia now fires at MarcarEnviado, the new cortacircuitos discard, registrarFallo's exhaustion DELETE, and descartarExpiradas; the defer and DELETE-error paths correctly HOLD the marker because the row survives for a later attempt. (b) The handoff still transmits exactly once: the claim writes id_mensaje_traspaso before Encolar, so at drain time SalidaPermitida returns true for that id and only that id. (c) The test is not fake-green: TestDrenarDescartaFilaEncoladaAntesDeDispararseCortacircuitos reconstructs the exact scenario I flagged (reply admitted pre-trip, deferred behind the 3000ms latency floor with the presence marker held, trip, then drain) and asserts only the handoff transmits, the reply row is hard-deleted, the counter and event fire, AND PresenciasPendientesParaPruebas returns to 0.

FINDING 2 (inbound fail-open) CLOSED. traduccion.go adds exported atomic ContadorErroresCortacircuitos and the Observar error path now increments it, logs EventoErrorCortacircuitos, and returns BEFORE persisting or forwarding, so no automated reply can be generated while the trip state is unreadable. This matches the hard-error idiom already used elsewhere in procesarMensaje (resolution/encoding/persistence errors also return early). TestProcesarMensaje_Cortacircuitos_ErrorDeObservacion_FallaCerradoYNoReenvia proves it honestly: no persist, no forwarded event, counter incremented, event logged.

NO REGRESSION from FIX 2 on legitimate inbound flow: the early return sits inside the else-if branch, so it is unreachable when the message is a baja/STOP (that path is untouched), when detectorCortacircuito is nil, or when Observar succeeds; Observar also returns (false, nil) for a nil control. The only new drop condition is a genuine store error, and no in-memory marker has been acquired at that point in procesarMensaje, so nothing leaks on the early return.

CARRY-FORWARD RESIDUAL for the next child (not actionable here, mirrors how HEX-019-a handed this child the liberarPresencia residual): the PRE-EXISTING baja drain-discard block in intentarUno does NOT call liberarPresencia, unlike the new cortacircuitos discard right below it. A row whose presence was announced on an earlier deferred attempt and is then discarded by baja leaks its in-memory marker. This is HEX-019-a/baja territory, untouched by this diff and outside this contract's authorization, so it must not be fixed here.

OBSERVATION (low, safe direction): the breaker observation runs before construirIdDeduplicacion, so a whatsmeow redelivery of the same message can increment the repetition counter twice for one logical message and trip early. Same ordering as the pre-existing baja detector, and a spurious trip errs toward silence plus human handoff, which is the safe side under adr-0015.

ACCEPTED TRADEOFF (unchanged): claim-then-enqueue means a crash between the claim commit and the enqueue loses the handoff permanently rather than duplicating it. Correct for the ratified at-most-once requirement; silence is the safe side.

STILL VERIFIED CLEAN after the fixes: handoff text byte-exact, threshold 3, keywords humano/persona/agente/operador, STOP check neither relocated nor weakened with the breaker strictly ahead of it at the COSTURA, STOP precedence over the handoff tested, non-disable enforced by bounds plus the reflection guard, state in the identidad-owned cortacircuitos table via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with no existing table altered, raw epoch ms on read and write, no new dependencies, ipc/mensajes.go and docs/STATUS.md untouched, adr-0015 [causa documentada] mark present, no mass-sending vocabulary, absolute dates.

MINOR (no action): identidad.Almacen.Restablecer still has no non-test caller, which contract behavior rule 12 explicitly authorizes as a store-level primitive only. The cortacircuitos row retains ultimo_texto_normalizado per contact; growth is O(contacts) via the id_interno PK, not per-message.
